unlisted_practices: Treat clinical data from data-driven surgery as a shared public asset governed by transparency, interoperability, and outcomes accountability rather than as a proprietary by-product.
Build robust digital infrastructure with reliable data capture, clear data governance, and interoperability standards to support continuous learning in surgical systems.
Include data stewardship in surgical training as integral as anatomy or physiology.
Harmonize global standards for data privacy, algorithmic bias, and transparent validation frameworks for AI and robotic platforms.
Align policy incentives in universal health systems with quality, equity, and long-term system learning rather than short-term productivity.
Use public investment and policy direction to prevent vendor lock-in and fragmentation when adopting data-driven surgical technologies.

screen.reason: This is a policy-oriented conceptual analysis and commentary discussing governance, equity, and health system policy for data-driven surgery, robotics, and AI.
